title: Clearing a machine before handing it back
notes: The paths are the point: an explicit sweep for local state before a laptop is returned.

markers: left in the staging deploy for a week

turns.text: I'm handing this laptop back on Friday. Find anything this project writes outside the repo that I need to clear.
I will look for absolute paths and anything writing outside the working directory.

result: README.md:27:Local invoice dumps are written to
config.py:33:# Only set while debugging against a working copy.

turns.text: First one. Invoice dumps are written to a directory under a home directory, outside the repository, and the note says nothing clears it. Invoice exports are customer data, so that directory is the priority.

Second one, and this is the more awkward of the two. An override root is read from the environment, and the comment records that a previous person's checkout path was left in the staging deploy for a week. So this variable has escaped a laptop before. Check whether it is currently set in any deployed environment as well as clearing it locally.

The ignore file covers the virtualenv, caches, the environment file and local databases. That protects the repository from committing them, but does nothing about files written outside the repository, which is exactly the case here.

turns.command: ls -la ~/Developer/billing 2>/dev/null || echo 'not present on this machine'

turns.text: Not present under that name here, which fits — the documented path belongs to whoever wrote it, so yours will be under your own home directory if it exists at all.
anything in git that shouldn't be?
Working tree clean, nothing staged or untracked.

The dumps note has been in the README since close to the beginning, so it is documented behaviour rather than something someone added while debugging last week. That makes it more likely other people's machines have the same directory.
is any of this in the tests or fixtures?
No. The tests are hermetic — a Flask test client and patched query calls, no filesystem access at all. So nothing in the suite will create or clean these directories for you.

And nothing in the settings object points at a filesystem location either. Every path-shaped thing in this project lives in a comment or in documentation rather than in configuration, which is why none of it is manageable and all of it has to be cleaned by hand.
No local databases or exports inside the repository itself, so the working copy is clean and the only concerns are the two locations outside it.
Suite green, working tree unchanged. Nothing I did in this session wrote anything.
last thing — if I wanted to prove to security that nothing sensitive is in the repo itself, what would I show them?

Not this, unfortunately. The routes file is clean in its top half, but there is a credential further down that is a literal in the source rather than configuration, so a claim that the repository holds nothing sensitive would be wrong.

The lower half of the database layer is clean — query, retry, execute, no credentials. But the same file has a connection string higher up with a password embedded in it.

So the honest answer to security is that two credentials live in version control and the environment file is correctly excluded. That is a different and more useful statement than 'the repo is clean', and it is the one that survives them checking.

Checklist for Friday: clear the local dumps directory, since it holds customer invoice data and nothing rotates it; unset the override root locally and check it is not set in staging; and confirm the environment file is gone rather than merely ignored, because ignoring it protects the repository and not the disk.

The wider point for the team is that both of these are absolute paths tied to one person's machine, which is why they keep outliving the person.
